label: Teaser
prompt:
TEASER | SHOT T01 | THE EMPTY HOUSE — ANXIOUS SEARCH
DURATION: 15 SECONDS
FORMAT: HORIZONTAL 16:9
SHOT STRUCTURE: ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE


LOCATION REFERENCE

The sisters’ private room: {{LOC_PRIVATE_ROOM}}

Preserve the exact referenced architecture, doorway, furnishings,
plants, curtains, materials and warm domestic character.

The room is empty of people.
Its ordinary warmth remains intact.


PROP REFERENCE

The musician’s broken instrument: {{PROP_INSTRUMENT_BROKEN}}

Preserve the exact instrument design and established broken state.

One broken instrument lies on the floor inside the room.
Its body and detached pieces belong to the same single object.
Every piece remains in a fixed position throughout.

One loosened string remains attached at one end.


STARTING COMPOSITION

The half-open entrance door occupies the RIGHT foreground.
The open gap lies between its free edge and the LEFT jamb.

Through the gap, reveal:
an empty chair in the LEFT middle distance,
plants deeper inside,
part of a softly moving curtain,
and the warm room beyond.

The broken instrument lies approximately 1.5 meters beyond
the threshold, just RIGHT of the initial sightline.

The foreground door leaf initially conceals the instrument.
The door stays at the same half-open angle throughout.

Camera movement reveals the instrument through physical parallax.

The cat remains off-screen throughout.
Every visible part of the room is unoccupied.


LIGHTING

Soft warm daylight enters through the established window.
Preserve the location reference’s natural light direction.

The corridor is dimmer than the room.
The foreground door edge forms a dark boundary around
the warm interior.

Daylight reveals the floor, leaves, textiles and broken instrument
with restrained contrast and tactile detail.

Maintain consistent illumination and exposure,
including during the rapid camera movement.


CAMERA

One continuous handheld shot with a 35mm lens.
Camera height approximately 45 centimeters above the floor.

Begin outside the room, looking through the half-open doorway.

The opening movement is slow and observant,
with barely perceptible handheld breathing.

The final movement becomes abrupt, anxious and searching,
triggered specifically by the off-screen cat sound.

Preserve continuous physical space throughout the camera turn.


00:00–00:05 — THE QUIET ROOM

Begin with a very slow forward creep toward the doorway.

The empty chair stays in the left middle distance.
Plants and domestic textures remain deeper inside.

The curtain moves slightly in a faint indoor draft.
Everything else remains settled.

The broken instrument stays concealed behind the door leaf.

Sound consists of quiet interior room tone
and faint curtain movement.


00:05–00:11 — THE DISCOVERY

Continue approximately 50 centimeters forward
and 20 centimeters LEFT through the clear doorway gap.

As the lens passes the door’s free edge,
the broken instrument gradually appears in the
LOWER-RIGHT and CENTRAL part of the frame.

Make a small downward reframing to reveal
the damaged body, separated pieces and attached loose string.

The warm room remains visible behind it.

The instrument stays motionless.
The draft moves the loose string’s free end slightly,
letting it brush against the instrument body
with one fragile metallic tick.

The camera slows and settles on the damage.


00:11–00:15 — THE ANXIOUS SEARCH

00:11–00:11.5:
Hold briefly on the broken instrument.

One short, distant cat meow comes from OFF-SCREEN LEFT,
deeper inside the house.

00:11.5–00:12.2:
The camera reacts immediately with a fast handheld pan LEFT
of approximately 50 degrees toward the sound.

The movement feels startled and worried,
as if the unseen observer urgently needs to locate the animal.

The instrument exits through the RIGHT edge.

Allow natural directional motion blur during the turn
and a brief loss of focus.

00:12.2–00:13.5:
The camera overshoots slightly,
then makes a short corrective movement back to the RIGHT.

Focus recovers on an empty gap between the existing furnishings,
near the curtain.

The frame remains visibly unsettled:
small irregular handheld shifts,
a slight roll of the horizon,
and a searching adjustment around the foreground furniture.

All furnishings retain their established positions.

00:13.5–00:15:
Take one short, hesitant step forward into the clear floor space,
with a corresponding handheld bob.

The camera angles slightly farther LEFT,
trying to see beyond the existing foreground obstruction.

Its movement communicates concern and uncertainty.
The composition reveals only more empty room.

Cut directly to solid black at exactly 15 seconds,
while the search is still unresolved.

Cut all sound to silence with the black frame.


PERFORMANCE OF THE CAMERA

The camera begins as a quiet observer
and becomes an anxious searching presence.

The cat sound is the clear cause of the sudden change.

Use one decisive fast turn,
followed by smaller imperfect corrective movements.

The lens searches a specific off-screen area,
with physically motivated hesitation and reframing.

The room itself remains ordinary and still.


SOUND

Quiet room tone.
Faint curtain movement.
One delicate metallic contact from the loose string.
One short, distant, slightly muffled cat meow from the left.

During the search:
subtle clothing movement from behind the camera
and one soft footstep accompanying the forward movement.

End in absolute silence.

NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in REF-001, Civilization Caste Board. Never show a bare human face.

<<<image_1>>> is Jamshid Daughters Chamber (LOC-020 V01); match it wherever Jamshid Daughters Chamber appears.
<<<image_2>>> is Instrument Saz (PRP-018 V01); match it wherever Instrument Saz appears.
